transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore. It's really noticeable, especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and handle things... like paperwork, or sitting down to go over shared household plans. I just can't seem to get comfortable or stay still for it.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medication, especially an antipsychotic or anti-nausea drug, in the weeks before this restlessness began?
No, nothing like that. I haven't started any new medications or changed any doses recently. I'm definitely not taking any antipsychotics or anti-nausea drugs.
Can you tell me when this restlessness first started, and was it around the time something significant changed or happened in your life?

Well, it's been... I mean, it has been noticeably worse since I got married. That was about a year and five months ago. When our routines merged and we started having to manage a household together, that's when I really started noticing how hard it is for me to just sit still for it.

Besides feeling physically restless during these tasks, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about many different things—like work, finances, or relationships—on most days, even when you're not trying to sit still?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think I worry any more than anyone else does. It's not like my mind is constantly spinning with stress over finances or my relationship or anything like that. It’s really just... that physical feeling of needing to move, rather than feeling anxious or worried about things.
Thinking back to when you were a child or teenager, did you ever have similar trouble sitting still, staying focused, or feeling restless in school or other settings?

Yeah, I did. Looking back, this was definitely a thing even when I was in elementary school. I was always the girl with a completely messy desk, and I constantly forgot my permission slips. My teachers were always sending notes home saying I talked out of turn or that I just couldn't seem to stay seated. So, yeah, it's been around for a long time.
Do you notice this same restlessness and trouble focusing in other areas of your life right now, like at work or in social situations, or is it really just limited to home tasks?

It's definitely not just at home. It happens when I'm volunteering, too. I help out with a few local organizations, but lately... well, the fallout has been that people at home and in my volunteer circles just can't reliably count on me. I'll forget things I promised to do, or I just can't focus enough to get them done. I've actually had to step back from some of my volunteer responsibilities recently because I keep letting things fall through, even though I'm really trying hard not to. It's frustrating.

Symptoms persist into adulthood, are present across multiple settings (home, volunteer work), and cause functional impairment (loss of reliability, stepping back from volunteer roles).
